parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Particle A: $2g-T=2a$. Particle B: $T-3g\sin18^\circ=T-9.27=3a$. System: $2g-3g\sin18^\circ=2g-9.27=(2+3)a$ — M1. Apply Newton’s second law to either particle A, particle B or the system. Correct number of terms.

A and B correct, or system correct — A1.

$a=2.145898034$ $[5a=10.72949017]$ — M1. Attempt to find $a$ using equations with correct number of terms.

$v^2=2a\times0.45$ — M1. Use of constant acceleration equations with their $a$ not equal to $\pm g$ to find $v^2$ when A reaches the ground.

$v^2=2(2.145898034)(0.45)=1.931308\ldots$ $[v=1.389715162]$ — A1. Allow unsimplified.

$T=0$, $\pm3g\sin18^\circ=3a$ $[a=\pm3.0901699]$ — M1. Attempt to find $a$ for the motion of B when string becomes slack. Allow trigonometric-function error, no extra terms.

$0=1.93-2(3.09)s$ $[s=0.312]$ — M1. Use constant acceleration equations, using a new $a$ not equal to $\pm g$, to find the further distance $s$ travelled by B before coming to rest.

Total distance moved by B $=0.45+0.312=0.762\text{ m}$ — A1.

Alternative method for Question 7:

Attempt PE loss as A reaches the ground — M1. Allow trigonometric-function error.

PE loss $=2g(0.45)-3g(0.45)\sin18^\circ$ $[=4.82827]$ — A1. Correct unsimplified.

$2g(0.45)-3g(0.45)\sin18^\circ=\frac12(2+3)v^2$ — *M1. Apply work-energy equation as PE loss balances KE gain; allow sign error, trigonometric-function error, four terms implied.

Solve for $v^2$ — DM1.

$v^2=1.931308\ldots$ $[v=1.389715162]$ — A1.

PE gain $=3g\sin18^\circ\,s$ — M1. Attempt PE gain for B after string breaks; allow sign error, trigonometric-function mix-up; $s$ = extra distance travelled by B along the plane.

$\frac12\times3\times1.931308=3g\sin18^\circ\,s$ $[s=0.312]$ — M1. Apply the work–energy equation for B by balancing PE gain with KE loss, using two terms.

Total distance moved by B $=0.45+0.312=0.762\text{ m}$ — A1.

Total: 8
